Subject: Orchestrated dependency quarantine + staged rollback lattice for private node upgrades

Team —

Following our SEV review with Acme last week, they want a scheme that lets us patch runtime deps with minimal blast radius and a clear, automated rollback ladder. I sketched a lightweight "quarantine" model that combines temporary node cordons + dependency whitelisting. Key asks in this email:

- Confirm that the plan can be executed inside Acme's VPC with the private agent (no external egress except the control-plane channel).
- Review the proposed staged rollback lattice (attached) and call out any missing failure modes.
- Flag any prerequisites for July-like kernel patches (network driver quiesce, NVMe remount grace).

Attached: dependency-quarantine-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet of step gates + gating telemetry).

High level flow:
1) Preflight: snapshot KV caches, tag model pins for the window, publish override keys to KMS v2.
2) Quarantine window (T0): cordon 10% of the fleet, drain with enhanced KV TTL, enable binary diff install path.
3) Canaries (T+1h): run smoke and perf probes, validate prefix cache hit rates.
4) Staged ramp (T+3h): incrementally uncordon groups; on regression, activate rollback lattice: pinned container variant -> pinned quantized model -> fallback lighter model -> full rollback.

I put a first-pass checklist in the attachment. Marissa, can you sanity-check the telemetry gating thresholds? Ben, please add SRE runbook snippets for the rollback lattice. Amelia / Nate — if you have deployment blackout rules or calendar constraints from Acme side, call them out.

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Orchestrated dependency quarantine + staged rollback lattice for private node upgrades

Thanks for the outline, Soo. Quick read-through — this is headed in the right direction. A few practical notes:

- Telemetry gating: the checklist's perf thresholds look conservative for Acme's peak (95th token latency +15% is too tight). Recommend 95th + 25% for the first ramp, and tighten on subsequent ramps if stable.
- KV cache snapshot: we should add an explicit verification that prefix cache snapshots are restorable in the staging VPC before the window. I added a column in the spreadsheet.
- Maintenance windows: Acme prefers a Tue/Thu 0200-0600 PST window. Amelia — is that still accurate?

Attachment: updated dependency-quarantine-checklist.xlsx (see column F: "restorability-tested").

Two operational asks for Ben and Jonas:
1) Ben — add the exact SRE playbook snippet for "force-evict KV cache" to the rollback doc. We need the command and the expected telemetry recovery curve.
2) Jonas — please confirm any network ACL constraints in Acme's subnets so we don't rely on ephemeral egress.

Marissa

Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 13:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Orchestrated dependency quarantine + staged rollback lattice for private node upgrades

Adding the SRE runbook snippets and some concrete failure-mode tests. I attached sre-rollback-snippets.md with the commands we will run in each lattice step. Highlights:

- Rollback ladder commands (examples):
  * switch-container: redwoodctl deploy set --node-group $G --image redwood/runtime:pinned-2026-11-02
  * force-evict-kv: redwoodctl kv evict --prefix "model_cache/" --dry-run (then without --dry-run)
  * switch-model-variant: redwoodctl model pin --model-id $MID --variant quantized-8bit

- Probe failures: the playbook defines two mandatory circuit breakers: 1) sustained 95th latency degradation for 15m, and 2) error-rate > 3% for 10m. Either trips the lattice to the previous stable rung.
- Backstop: if automated rollback fails twice within 2 hours, the playbook recommends a full fleet rollback and a fast incident bridge with Acme.

Ben

Attachments: sre-rollback-snippets.md

--
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Dedicated & Private

Thanks — this looks thorough. A few notes from Acme ops:

- Maintenance window confirmed: Tue/Thu 02:00-06:00 PST. We prefer the first attempt to target the smaller customer-facing tier (10% of the fleet) and validate before expanding.
- No external egress allowed except to "%control.redwood.internal" on port 443; ensure the agent uses the pinned CA.
- We ran a short simulation of the KV snapshot restore last night; outcome: restore succeeded but TTL skewed by ~120s on a test host. Please add a 2-minute buffer to any timing assumptions in runbook steps.

We'll provision an internal standup channel and a shared folder for logs. I uploaded our acceptance checklist to the Drive link you included and added a comment on row F in the spreadsheet.

Amelia

Ops Lead, Acme Logistics
ops@acme-logistics.com
